claim: N/P ratio of the cytotoxicity experiment
locus_A: SI p.5, 'Cytotoxicity evaluation of 1-O16B/siRNA complex': '1-O16B/siRNA(N/P = 2:1) complexes'
locus_B: SI p.9, Fig S3 caption: '1-O16B and siGFP was mixed at N/P ratios of 5:1'
why: The same experiment is given two N/P ratios in the same document. Not resolvable from the SI; no third statement exists. Irrelevant to what we emit because the panel is a viability assay and is inadmissible anyway, but it is recorded because it bears on how much the SI's other unduplicated numbers can be trusted.

claim: siRNA concentration range of the 1-O16B dose series
locus_A: SI p.5: 'the final concentration of siRNA increased from 0.25nM to 8nM'
locus_B: SI p.9, Fig S3 x-axis: 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 nM
why: The viability sweep (1-32 nM) and the efficacy sweep (0.25-8 nM) overlap on only 1, 2, 4 and 8 nM. Not a contradiction -- two different experiments -- but recorded so nobody later reads Fig S3 as the toxicity arm of the efficacy curve. Four of six viability doses have no efficacy counterpart.

locus_B: computed: neutral average 767.331; neutral monoisotopic 766.484; [M+H]+ monoisotopic 767.492; [M+H]+ average 768.369
why: 'Calcd' is the NEUTRAL AVERAGE mass (residuals 0.031 and 0.029 Da, next-best candidate 0.16 and 0.44 Da away), but an ESI-MS peak is necessarily an ION, so the printed Calcd and the printed Found are not the same quantity. Found - neutral average is +0.369 and +0.529 Da. The instrument therefore confirms the molecular FORMULA at about unit resolution and nothing finer; no sub-Dalton claim should be made from it. See QC P4.

locus_B: SI p.2: 'Dimitri Pouli'; PubMed/Europe PMC: 'Pouli D'
why: Cosmetic, on the same document's two cover pages. Recorded only to show the metadata was read rather than copied.

claim: which formulation a measurement belongs to
locus_A: SI p.3 screening: 'crude lipidoids (3.2 ug)' mixed with siRNA in acetate buffer, NO helper lipid named
locus_B: SI p.4 CLSM: 'lipidoid, cholesterol, and DOPE were mixed in chloroform at weight ratios of 16:4:1'
why: This paper uses at least two different formulations -- bare crude lipidoid for the flow-cytometry screen, and a 16:4:1 w/w lipidoid/cholesterol/DOPE film for the imaging work. If the main article is ever acquired, its panels must be assigned to the right one; pooling them would put two formulations under one Formulation_ID.

claim: RETRACTED SUSPICION: that 'O16B' denotes a C16 S-alkyl
locus_A: the name token itself, by analogy with O16 = hexadecyl
locus_B: SI p.3: ESI-MS C39H78N2O4S4, and the 1H NMR bulk-methylene integral of 40H
why: Kept because it is the error this nomenclature invites and because it was the working hypothesis until measured. A C16 S-alkyl gives C47H94N2O4S4 (8 carbons too many) and predicts a 56H bulk integral against the printed 40H. TWO independent printed facts reject it. The token counts CHAIN HEAVY ATOMS: 2 C + 2 S + 12 C = 16, which is also the only reading that makes the paper's own 'similar chemical structures' claim true.

claim: RETRACTED SUSPICION: that the '1' in '1-O16' is the corpus's amine 1
locus_A: the corpus contains AA_2008 lipidoids named 1_O10 ... 1_O18 with the same O<n> acrylate suffix
locus_B: AA_2008's amine 1 is 3-methoxypropylamine: its 1_O15 is C40H79NO5, ONE nitrogen and FIVE oxygens, against the SI's printed C43H86N2O4
why: Kept because keying on the leading number token would have put every value in this paper on a molecule the paper's own mass spectrum excludes. The printed formula rejects it on BOTH the nitrogen and the oxygen count. Xu's 'amine 1' is in fact the Anderson/Akinc catalogue's amine 80, confirmed by head-InChIKey identity with AA_2008's 80_O10/80_O15/80_O18 (QC P6, 3/3).
